summary: This article explains why the narrow Strait of Hormuz, which links the Persian Gulf to the open sea, is one of the busiest and most important shipping routes on Earth.
introduce: Drop a pencil and ask, “What was the cause? What was the effect?” to model the idea quickly. Then show the title “The Strait of Hormuz: A Vital Waterway” and tell students to look for things in the article that make other things happen.

keyTerms.def: describing oil that has not yet been cleaned or processed
a marked path that ships or vehicles must stay within
a path or way followed to get from one place to another

challengeTerms.def: a narrow passage through which a large share of trade or traffic must travel
to take or pull something out, especially from the ground
the total amount of something, especially goods or traffic

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a narrow strip of water can matter more to world trade than a huge ocean? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why the Strait of Hormuz matters for the world's energy supply.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review crude, lane, and route, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses chokepoint, extract, and volume to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
